items.title: 66095_Benny Carter oral history interview
items.q: - was a successor to Jim Europe.

ctx.x: So I got the C Melody and brought it home, and Harold Hal Proctor taught me for a little while; he taught me how to play the instrument, as far as he felt he could take me, and then he suggested I go to a teacher -- a real teacher -- because Harold Hal Proctor did not read music, as I said. So then I went to this Lieutenant Michael, and I started studying with him. At first, he turned me over to his star pupil, who was very advanced, and his name was Rudy Powell, and then I studied with him for a little while,…

Okay. Does this sound plausible -- this comes from a booklet that was written by George Hoefer in the Jazz Odyssey series, and actually in the third volume called "The Sound of Harlem" and he says in these notes, I believe this is pretty close to a quote, that Eugene Michael -- spelled MIKELL -- was a successor to Jim Europe.
